sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: This perennial foxglove grows in open woodland and woodland margins of central and eastern Europe. It forms a clump about 60–90 cm tall and 30–45 cm wide.

sections.title: Flowering
sections.text: In summer, cream-yellow tubular flowers with brown veins inside open along an upright stem. They are paler than those of the common foxglove (Digitalis purpurea).

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: Like other foxgloves, it contains cardiac glycosides and must not be eaten. All parts are considered poisonous.
